# pg_atropos

> Split PostgreSQL custom-format (`pg_dump -Fc`) dumps into individual files organized for Git versioning.

pg_atropos is a CLI tool written in Go that takes a single PostgreSQL custom-format dump and cuts it into one file per database object (tables, functions, indexes, roles, …). Instead of parsing raw SQL text with brittle regexes, it pipes the dump through `pg_restore -f -` and relies on the clean `-- Name: ...; Type: ...` headers to detect object boundaries. The result is minimal merge conflicts, readable diffs and per-object Git history.

## Key Facts

- Language: Go (standard library only, no external dependencies)
- Requires: `pg_restore` (PostgreSQL client tools)
- Input: custom-format dump file, stdin (`-f -`), or a live database (`--db` / `--conn`)
- License: MIT
- Install: `brew install heptau/tap/pg-atropos` or build from source (`make build`)
- Platforms: macOS, Linux, Windows (amd64, arm64), Docker

## Quick start

```bash
brew install heptau/tap/pg-atropos
pg_dump -Fc mydb | pg_atropos -f - -o ./structure
```

## Typical use cases

- Versioning a PostgreSQL schema in Git with one file per object
- Code review of schema changes (diff shows only the changed object)
- Per-object history (`git log -- TABLE/users.sql`)
- CI/CD pipelines that deploy only changed objects
